title: Tumour Genotype and Targeted Drugs: EGFR, RAS and ALK
summary: Match tumour mutations to targeted drugs: EGFR exon 19 deletions and L858R predict TKI response, T790M causes acquired resistance treated with osimertinib, RAS mutations rule out anti-EGFR antibodies in colorectal cancer, and ALK fusions point to crizotinib.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 75 Hits 7, 8 and 13 and Exam Traps 3 and 4. Checked against Ricciuti 2017, Sullivan 2016, Sepulveda 2017 (ASCP/CAP/AMP/ASCO CRC guideline), Golding 2018, Du 2018 and Fisher 2012. Differences: exon 19 deletions plus L858R are about 85–90% of EGFR mutations in both reviews read (reviewer: > 90%); T790M explains about 50% (Sullivan) to 60% (Ricciuti) of acquired resistance; the 2017 guideline found insufficient evidence to use BRAF as a predictive marker for anti-EGFR response (reviewer: BRAF → anti-EGFR resistance). Not taught: FDA labelling statements for anti-EGFR antibodies; the 10–30% dramatic-response figure; per-mutation shares (~45% each). The CAP/IASLC/AMP lung testing guideline (Lindeman 2013/2018) had no open full text and was not read.

objectives: Name the EGFR mutations that predict response or resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
Explain why T790M calls for osimertinib rather than another first-generation TKI.
Apply extended RAS testing rules before anti-EGFR antibodies in colorectal cancer.
Recognise EML4-ALK detection by break-apart FISH and its drug class.

scenes.title: Three tumours, three reports
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three molecular reports arrive. (1) Lung adenocarcinoma with an EGFR exon 19 deletion, treated with erlotinib for a year, now progressing; the new biopsy shows EGFR T790M. (2) Metastatic colorectal cancer, KRAS exon 2 not mutated but an NRAS exon 3 codon 61 mutation; the oncologist asks about cetuximab. (3) Lung adenocarcinoma, EGFR not mutated, ALK break-apart FISH showing split signals in 30% of tumour cells. Question token: “Which drug fits, and which will fail?”

cues.text: Three molecular reports arrive. A lung cancer that responded to erlotinib is growing again, and the new biopsy shows EGFR T790M.
A colorectal cancer has normal KRAS exon 2 but a mutation in NRAS exon 3. Can it get cetuximab? And a lung cancer shows split ALK signals.
For each tumour: which drug fits, and which one will fail?

props.label: Which drug fits, and which will fail?

scenes.title: EGFR and the drugs that block it
scenes.altText: Schematic receptor: EGFR spans the cell membrane with an outer ligand-binding domain and an inner tyrosine kinase domain. Card 1: antibodies (cetuximab, panitumumab) bind the outer domain and block ligand binding. Card 2: tyrosine kinase inhibitors work inside the cell; first-generation gefitinib and erlotinib bind reversibly, second-generation afatinib irreversibly. Card 3: activating mutations sit in the kinase domain, exons 18 to 21; EGFR mutations are found in about 10–17% of NSCLC in North America and Europe and about 30–50% in Asian countries, more often in women, never-smokers and adenocarcinoma, but clinical features cannot rule them out. Card 4: RAS lies downstream of the receptor.

cues.text: The epidermal growth factor receptor, EGFR, has an outer domain that binds growth factors and an inner tyrosine kinase that sends the signal on.
Two drug types block it. Antibodies such as cetuximab and panitumumab bind the outer domain. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as gefitinib and erlotinib act on the kinase inside the cell.

In lung cancer, activating mutations sit in the kinase domain, exons eighteen to twenty-one. They are found in about ten to seventeen percent of cases in North America and Europe and up to half in Asian countries, more often in women, never-smokers and adenocarcinoma.
Clinical features cannot rule a mutation out, so the tumour is tested. And remember RAS: it sits downstream of the receptor.

scenes.title: Sensitizing, resistant, and the gatekeeper
scenes.altText: Left card: sensitizing mutations — exon 19 in-frame deletions (E746–A750) and exon 21 L858R together account for about 85–90% of EGFR mutations in NSCLC and predict response to EGFR TKIs. Exon 20 insertions cause primary resistance. Right card: acquired resistance appears after about 9–14 months; the exon 20 T790M “gatekeeper” mutation in the ATP-binding pocket explains about 50–60% of cases and blocks first- and second-generation TKIs. Token: osimertinib, an irreversible third-generation TKI that binds covalently at C797 and inhibits sensitizing and T790M mutants; US FDA approval November 2015 for T790M-positive NSCLC after progression on an earlier EGFR TKI, with the cobas EGFR Mutation Test v2. Later resistance can come from C797S.

cues.text: Two mutations dominate: in-frame deletions in exon 19 and the L858R point mutation in exon 21. Together they make up about eighty-five to ninety percent of EGFR mutations, and they predict response to the inhibitors.
Not every EGFR mutation helps. Exon 20 insertions cause primary resistance: the drug fails from the start.

Responders relapse, typically within nine to fourteen months. In about half to sixty percent of cases the cause is T790M in exon 20, the gatekeeper residue in the ATP pocket, which stops first- and second-generation drugs from working.

Osimertinib, a third-generation irreversible inhibitor, blocks both the sensitizing mutation and T790M. The US FDA approved it in November 2015 for T790M-positive disease after an earlier EGFR inhibitor. Later, the C797S mutation can make it fail too.

scenes.title: Colorectal RAS and lung ALK
scenes.altText: Card 1, colorectal cancer (ASCP/CAP/AMP/ASCO 2017): patients considered for anti-EGFR antibodies must have RAS testing — KRAS and NRAS exon 2 (codons 12, 13), exon 3 (59, 61) and exon 4 (117, 146), “extended RAS”; RAS-mutant tumours gain no significant benefit. BRAF V600 testing is recommended for prognosis and Lynch syndrome evaluation; evidence was judged insufficient to use BRAF as a predictive marker for anti-EGFR response. Card 2, ALK: EML4-ALK arises from an inversion on chromosome 2p and occurs in about 3–7% of NSCLC, usually not together with EGFR or KRAS mutations. Vysis break-apart FISH was the first FDA-approved test: positive when more than 15% of tumour cells show split red and green signals more than two signal diameters apart or an isolated red signal. Crizotinib (FDA 2011); after resistance, ceritinib or alectinib. Hook answers: (1) osimertinib, not another first-generation TKI; (2) no cetuximab — NRAS-mutant; (3) ALK-positive → ALK inhibitor such as crizotinib.

cues.text: In colorectal cancer, any patient considered for an anti-EGFR antibody must have extended RAS testing: KRAS and NRAS, exons two, three and four. A RAS mutation means no significant benefit from cetuximab or panitumumab.
BRAF V600 is tested for prognosis and to help sort out Lynch syndrome. In the 2017 guideline, the evidence was not strong enough to use BRAF to predict anti-EGFR response.

In lung cancer, an inversion on chromosome two fuses EML4 to ALK, in about three to seven percent of cases. On break-apart FISH, more than fifteen percent of tumour cells with split or isolated red signals is positive, pointing to crizotinib, then ceritinib or alectinib after resistance.
Back to the hook. T790M: switch to osimertinib. The NRAS-mutant colorectal cancer: no cetuximab. The ALK-positive lung cancer: an ALK inhibitor.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “T790M after erlotinib: switch to gefitinib” (✓ first-generation TKIs share the T790M problem; use osimertinib); “The tumour expresses EGFR, so cetuximab works even with a KRAS mutation” (✓ RAS mutation means no significant anti-EGFR benefit); “KRAS exon 2 normal = RAS wild-type” (✓ extended RAS: KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3 and 4).

cues.text: Trap one: after T790M on erlotinib, try gefitinib. No: both are first-generation drugs blocked by the gatekeeper. Use osimertinib.
Trap two: the colorectal tumour has EGFR, so cetuximab will work despite a KRAS mutation. No: a RAS mutation means no significant benefit.
Trap three: KRAS exon 2 is normal, so the tumour is RAS wild-type. No: test KRAS and NRAS exons two, three and four.

scenes.title: Doorbell, gatekeeper, stuck switch
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “EGFR is a doorbell. Antibodies tape over the button outside; TKIs cut the wire inside. Exon 19 and 21 mutations jam the bell on, and the wire cutter works. T790M is a new gatekeeper that blocks the old cutters, so bring osimertinib. If RAS, further down the wire, is stuck on, taping the button does nothing.” Tokens: button = antibody · wire = TKI · stuck below = RAS. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: EGFR is a doorbell. Antibodies tape over the outside button; kinase inhibitors cut the wire inside. T790M is a gatekeeper that blocks the old cutters. And if RAS, further down the wire, is stuck on, taping the button does nothing.
Where it breaks: uncommon EGFR mutations, such as exon 18 G719X, may also respond; T790M is not the only resistance route; and BRAF evidence in colorectal cancer is less clear-cut than RAS.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Exon 19 deletion · L858R → EGFR TKI; T790M → osimertinib”, “Colorectal: extended RAS wild-type before anti-EGFR · ALK fusion → crizotinib”.

cues.text: EGFR exon 19 deletions and L858R predict response to EGFR kinase inhibitors, acquired T790M calls for osimertinib, colorectal cancer needs extended RAS wild-type status before cetuximab or panitumumab, and an ALK fusion points to an ALK inhibitor such as crizotinib.

props.label: Exon 19 del · L858R → EGFR TKI · T790M → osimertinib
Colorectal: extended RAS wild-type first · ALK fusion → crizotinib

explanation.what: Plain language: some cancers grow because one signalling protein is stuck on, and a drug that blocks that protein can work dramatically, but only if the tumour truly depends on it and has not found a way around it. The lab’s mutation report decides which drug is worth giving. Scientific terms: epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), sensitizing mutation (exon 19 deletion, L858R), primary resistance (exon 20 insertion), acquired resistance, gatekeeper mutation (T790M), osimertinib, anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody (cetuximab, panitumumab), extended RAS testing (KRAS and NRAS exons 2–4), BRAF V600, EML4-ALK fusion, break-apart FISH, crizotinib.
explanation.why: TKIs bind the EGFR kinase domain; the T790 residue sits in the ATP-binding pocket, and T790M blocks first- and second-generation drugs, while osimertinib binds covalently at C797. Anti-EGFR antibodies bind the receptor’s outer domain and block ligand binding; KRAS lies in the downstream pathway, and tumours with activating KRAS or NRAS mutations gain no significant benefit from these antibodies.
explanation.measure: EGFR mutations: ~10–17% of NSCLC in North America/Europe, ~30–50% in Asia; exon 19 deletion + L858R ~85–90% of them. Acquired resistance after ~9–14 months; T790M in ~50–60%. Osimertinib: US FDA approval November 2015 (T790M-positive, after prior EGFR TKI). CRC: RAS testing must include KRAS and NRAS codons 12/13 (exon 2), 59/61 (exon 3), 117/146 (exon 4). ALK: ~3–7% of NSCLC; Vysis break-apart FISH positive if > 15% of tumour cells show split (> 2 signal diameters) or isolated red signals; crizotinib FDA 2011; Ventana ALK (D5F3) IHC companion test 2015; ceritinib and alectinib were first used after crizotinib resistance and were later also approved as first-line therapy (US).
explanation.differs: Sensitizing (exon 19 del, L858R) vs resistant (exon 20 insertion, T790M); TKI (kinase domain, inside) vs antibody (outer domain); RAS (negative predictor for anti-EGFR antibodies) vs BRAF V600 in CRC (prognostic; predictive value judged insufficient in 2017). BRAF V600E in melanoma is different again: the US licensed indication for the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib is BRAF V600E-mutant advanced melanoma.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: choose osimertinib after T790M, refuse cetuximab for any KRAS or NRAS mutation, recognise that KRAS exon 2 alone is not enough, and link EML4-ALK FISH to crizotinib.

questions.stem: A patient with EGFR exon 19-deleted lung adenocarcinoma responds to erlotinib for 12 months, then progresses. A new biopsy shows EGFR T790M. Which drug is most appropriate next?

options.rationale: Correct. This third-generation irreversible TKI inhibits both the sensitizing mutation and T790M.
Incorrect. Gefitinib is a first-generation TKI; T790M blocks it just as it blocks erlotinib.
Incorrect. Cetuximab is an anti-EGFR antibody that binds the outer domain; the drug designed for T790M-positive progression is osimertinib.

options.text: Continue erlotinib at a higher dose
options.rationale: Incorrect. T790M is a resistance mechanism; the tumour is already progressing on erlotinib.

questions.stem: A metastatic colorectal cancer has no mutation in KRAS exon 2 but carries an NRAS exon 3 codon 61 mutation. What does this mean for cetuximab or panitumumab?

options.text: No significant benefit is expected; the tumour is RAS-mutant
options.rationale: Correct. Extended RAS testing includes NRAS exons 2–4, and any RAS mutation is a negative predictor for anti-EGFR antibodies.

options.text: Benefit is expected because KRAS exon 2 is wild-type
options.rationale: Incorrect. KRAS exon 2 alone is not enough; the guideline requires KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3 and 4.

options.text: Benefit is expected because the tumour expresses EGFR
options.rationale: Incorrect. The guideline selects patients by RAS mutation status, not by EGFR on the tumour; RAS-mutant tumours gain no significant benefit.

options.text: BRAF must be mutated before the drugs can be given
options.rationale: Incorrect. BRAF V600 testing is recommended for prognosis and Lynch evaluation, not as a requirement for anti-EGFR therapy.

questions.stem: An NSCLC specimen is tested with an ALK break-apart FISH probe. Which result is reported as ALK-rearranged?

options.text: More than 15% of tumour cells show red and green signals split by more than two signal diameters, or an isolated red signal
options.rationale: Correct. This is the positive pattern for the Vysis break-apart assay.

options.text: All tumour cells show fused red-green signals
options.rationale: Incorrect. A positive result needs split or isolated red signals in more than 15% of tumour cells; signals that stay together do not show this pattern.

options.text: Split signals in 5% of tumour cells
options.rationale: Incorrect. This is below the more-than-15% threshold.

options.text: An EGFR exon 19 deletion on sequencing
options.rationale: Incorrect. That is an EGFR result; ALK fusions are usually found without EGFR mutations.

references.usedFor: Activating mutations in kinase domain exons 18–21; 10–17% (North America/Europe) and 30–50% (Asia); exon 19 deletion + L858R ~85–90%; resistance after 9–13 months; T790M in about 50% of cases.

references.citation: Sepulveda AR, Hamilton SR, Allegra CJ, et al. Molecular Biomarkers for the Evaluation of Colorectal Cancer. Am J Clin Pathol. 2017;147(3):221-260.
references.usedFor: Guideline statement 1 (RAS testing must be done before anti-EGFR therapy; KRAS and NRAS codons 12/13, 59/61, 117/146); no significant anti-EGFR benefit with KRAS/NRAS mutations; cetuximab and panitumumab bind the EGFR extracellular domain; statements 2a/2b (BRAF V600 for prognosis and Lynch evaluation); statement 4 (insufficient evidence for BRAF as a predictive marker); BRAF-mutant tumours showed decreased response rate.

references.citation: Golding B, Luu A, Jones R, Viloria-Petit AM. The function and therapeutic targeting of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mol Cancer. 2018;17(1):52.
references.usedFor: EML4-ALK from an inversion on chromosome 2p; ALK rearrangements in 3–7% of NSCLC, mutually exclusive with KRAS and EGFR mutations; Vysis break-apart FISH as the first FDA-approved test and its > 15% positivity criteria; ceritinib and alectinib after crizotinib resistance and their later first-line approvals (ceritinib May 2017, alectinib November 2017).

references.citation: Du X, Shao Y, Qin HF, Tai YH, Gao HJ. ALK-rearrangement in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Thorac Cancer. 2018;9(4):423-430.
references.usedFor: Crizotinib FDA approval in 2011 for ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC; FISH as reference method; Ventana ALK (D5F3) IHC approved as companion test in 2015; ceritinib and alectinib approved in the US.

claims.text: EGFR structure and drug sites; mutation frequency and associations; exons 18–21; exon 19 deletion + L858R ~85–90%; exon 20 insertions resistant.
Acquired resistance timing; T790M ~50–60%, gatekeeper; osimertinib mechanism and November 2015 FDA approval; C797S.
Extended RAS testing before anti-EGFR antibodies; no significant benefit in RAS-mutant CRC; RAS downstream of EGFR.
BRAF V600 in CRC: prognostic and Lynch evaluation; insufficient evidence as anti-EGFR predictor (2017); vemurafenib for BRAF V600E melanoma.
EML4-ALK inversion 2p, 3–7%, mutual exclusivity; break-apart FISH criteria; IHC 2015; crizotinib 2011; ceritinib/alectinib after crizotinib resistance and later first-line.
FDA labels requiring RAS wild-type by an FDA-approved test; exon 19 ~45% and L858R ~40–45% individually; gefitinib/erlotinib dramatic response in 10–30%; BRAF as anti-EGFR resistance marker.
claims.note: Not taught as stated; not supported by the passages read (or qualified by Sepulveda 2017 for BRAF).

claims.text: Scenario invented; receptor and FISH drawings schematic.

accuracyFlags.issue: Hit 7 says exon 19 deletions plus L858R are > 90% of EGFR mutations; Ricciuti 2017 and Sullivan 2016 both give about 85–90%. The lesson teaches 85–90% (register flag rv-egfr-common-share).
Hit 7 gives T790M as 50% of acquired resistance; Sullivan 2016 says about 50%, Ricciuti 2017 about 60% (68% with a more sensitive LNA-PCR assay). The lesson teaches about 50–60%.

Hit 8 and Trap 4 call BRAF mutation an anti-EGFR resistance marker; the 2017 ASCP/CAP/AMP/ASCO guideline found insufficient evidence to recommend BRAF V600 as a predictive marker (decreased response rate, but data consistent with modest benefit relative to RAS-mutant tumours). Later evidence was not reviewed (register flag rv-crc-braf-predictive).

FDA approvals and companion diagnostics (osimertinib 2015, crizotinib 2011, Vysis FISH, Ventana IHC) are US regulatory facts; Philippine FDA registration and practice are not covered (register flag rv-ch75-us-approvals).

morphology.note: No micrographs or FISH images; receptor and signals shown as cards.
